rag.title: Evidence path
steps: Authenticate the caller and identify the task.
Search current authorized chunks with metadata filters.
Send bounded evidence and instructions to the model.
Check source support, citations, schema, and safety.

secure-rag.title: Tenant boundary
steps: Derive tenant and role on the server.
Apply source permissions before the model sees evidence.
Use approved model, prompt, and safety policy.
Validate evidence and restrict logs and caches.

ingest.title: Source to index
steps: S3, connector, or approved enterprise change event.
Parse text and tables. Check data quality and permissions.
Preserve source version and use a compatible embedding model.
Upsert or delete vectors. Measure freshness and ingestion errors.

gateway.title: Governed model access
steps: Authenticate and derive trusted access context.
Validate requests and enforce budgets and policy.
Apply compatible schema, prompt version, and model route.
Correlate model use, evidence, quality, and cost.

resilience.title: Controlled failure path
steps: Distinguish invalid input, denied access, throttle, and transient fault.
Use bounded jittered retries and a circuit breaker.
Preserve quality, residency, permissions, and user-visible status.
resilience.relation: This path applies after a failure. A successful invocation returns normally.

vector.title: Semantic retrieval
steps: Embed each permitted chunk and preserve source metadata.
Apply access filters and compare vectors or hybrid scores.
Return passages with references. Score meaning remains model-specific.
vector.relation: Document and query encoders are independent inputs to candidate search. They must share a compatible embedding contract.

chunk.title: Parent and child context
steps: Keep sections, tables, and source locations intact.
Embed smaller passages for precise candidate matches.
Replace matching children with broader parents where configured.
Deduplicate context and reserve output tokens.

rerank.title: Two-stage retrieval
steps: Preserve intent, exact terms, and data access scope.
Use vector or hybrid search to obtain relevant candidates.
Score the available candidates against the query.
Select supported evidence within the prompt budget.

chat.title: Conversation state
steps: Verify ownership and load required structured constraints.
Select recent history, tested summaries, and evidence.
Use approved instructions and a bounded token budget.
Validate the result and store only permitted state.

workflow.title: Fixed document workflow
steps: Convert the supported document into fields and evidence.
Check schema, required values, and source support.
Route exceptions to review under explicit rules.
Write authorized results and record the operation.

agent.title: Agent action loop
steps: Use task state and available tool schemas.
Validate identity, parameters, budget, and any required approval.
Call the tool with retry safety. Record the result.
Update state. Enforce success, step limit, and deadline.
agent.relation: If more work remains, repeat from stage 1 within enforced budgets. Otherwise stop.

multiagent.title: Specialist coordination
steps: Split the task and enforce shared constraints.
Use narrow task contracts and scoped tool access.
Compare findings and resolve conflicting evidence.
Evaluate the combined result and total task cost.
multiagent.relation: Specialists can run in parallel when their tasks are independent. The supervisor still validates the combined result.

approval.title: Controlled transaction
steps: Prepare the exact operation from current authorized evidence.
Check business rules, actor scope, amount, and parameters.
Bind human approval to the exact action and expiry.
Use an idempotency key and confirm transaction status.

tool.title: Tool trust boundary
steps: Validate schema, permissions, business rules, and destination.
Execute with deadline and side-effect safeguards.
Return a typed result or classified failure.

mcp.title: MCP tool access
steps: Discover tools through the supported protocol.
Expose explicit names, schemas, and controlled capabilities.
Resolve identity and restrict resource and operation scope.
Call the approved API and return verified results.

agentcore.title: AgentCore responsibilities
steps: Execute the selected agent framework in a supported environment.
Connect approved tools with suitable identity controls.
Maintain permitted task and user state.
Trace task behavior, tool operations, latency, and failures.
agentcore.relation: These are component responsibilities. Select and connect the components that the application requires.

cascade.title: Conditional model escalation
steps: Identify required capability and hard constraints.
Use a smaller model for proven suitable tasks.
Invoke an approved capable path when the validated small path cannot satisfy the task.
Compare total task quality, latency, and cost.
cascade.relation: Escalation is conditional. A successful small-model path can return without a larger-model call.

async.title: Durable async request
steps: Validate the task and return an operation identifier.
Apply backpressure and perform supported inference work.
Persist status and output with access controls.
Poll or receive an approved notification of completion.

stream.title: End-to-end streaming
steps: Receive supported content blocks and completion events.
Track state, safety checks, cancellation, and errors.
Use a compatible unbuffered integration and client protocol.
Show partial output and distinguish final validated content.

safety.title: Defense in depth
steps: Check harmful content and indirect instruction attacks.
Use supported safety policies and bounded instructions.
Enforce permission and validate every side effect.
Check policy, sensitive data, structure, and evidence.
safety.relation: Apply these controls at each relevant boundary. No single filter replaces authorization.

private.title: Private inference path
steps: Use a role and private subnet network controls.
Configure security groups, private DNS, and endpoint policy.
Authorize the exact model or approved inference profile.
Use separate access and encryption controls for sources and logs.
private.relation: These are separate access boundaries. The application can call data services independently of Bedrock.

pii.title: Sensitive data lifecycle
steps: Classify source data and locate sensitive fields.
Redact or tokenize fields that the task does not require.
Use approved model access, permissions, and output policy.
Apply policy to sources, vectors, caches, histories, and logs.

cache.title: Cache lookup and miss path
steps: Resolve identity, source version, model, prompt, and policy.
Return a valid authorized hit. On a miss, continue to the model path.
Use supported prefix caching on a model invocation.
Invalidate eligible entries after data, permission, model, or policy changes.
cache.relation: A valid result hit returns immediately. Prefix reuse applies to a model call. Invalidation is a separate event.

latency.title: Request critical path
steps: Measure first token, completion time, and output length.
Measure downstream work and client delivery.

observe.title: Correlated operations
steps: Propagate correlation ID and version identifiers.
Record retrieval, model, and tool performance.
Evaluate sampled answers and task completion.
Alert the owner and execute tested remediation.
observe.relation: Collect these signals across the request path. They are not a mandatory sequence of API calls.

eval.title: Release quality gate
steps: Freeze model, prompt, retrieval, data, and tool settings.
Run task, safety, latency, and cost evaluations.
Compare required thresholds and critical failures.
Use canary or shadow validation and a rollback target.
